plan.summary:
New `Record` IDs use UUIDv7 instead of UUIDv4, so IDs sort by creation time.

- `Cargo.toml` swaps the `uuid` feature `v4` for `v7`.
- `Record::new` calls `Uuid::now_v7()` instead of `Uuid::new_v4()`.
- Existing records keep their old IDs.
- `Cargo.lock` changes follow the manifest change.
plan.riskRationale: Small change to ID generation. Old v4 IDs stay valid. Removing the `v4` feature breaks any other code that calls `new_v4`. The diff does not show such code.
plan.storyArc: The feature flag in the manifest enables the v7 generator. The `Record::new` constructor then uses it. The lockfile only records the new transitive dependencies.

topics.title: Record IDs use time-ordered UUIDv7
topics.narrativeBrief: How do new records get their IDs, and what must change in the manifest to allow it? Connect the `uuid` feature switch from `v4` to `v7` with the `Uuid::now_v7()` call in `Record::new`. Verify no other code in the crate still needs `v4`.
